long_biography.plain_text:
Alejo Peralta built the industrial group that Carlos Peralta Quintero would later inherit and expand. Carlos began as a mechanical-shop apprentice and moved through production, administration and senior management. He then developed Iusacell within the family group, brought in Bell Atlantic and took the mobile operator to public markets in New York and Mexico.

Peralta succeeded his father as IUSA chairman in 1997. Its current manufacturing base includes electrical conductors, copper products, power equipment, meters, valves and controls, with plants in Mexico and the United States. His board role now sits above a separate director general, while he remains active as foundation president and chairman of the Jaguares de Nayarit baseball club.

uncertainties.detail: No reliable public source located links Carlos Peralta Quintero specifically to Pantala. Identity is nevertheless resolved because the source record's exact name, nationality and age align with institutional biographical data, while Forbes independently connects that same exact-name IUSA chairman to superyacht ownership. Vessel evidence is excluded from the biographies.

The Mexican Stock Exchange labels Peralta a patrimonial board member and chairman, and public reporting frequently describes the family group as his. No current reliable source discloses his exact personal percentage in IUSA or its subsidiaries, so company assets are not presented as personally titled holdings.

Some business profiles continue to call Peralta IUSA's president and director general. The current Mexican Stock Exchange issuer profile instead lists him as board chairman and names Antonio Garcia Herranz as director general; the dossier uses the exchange's clearer governance distinction.

Iusacell is historically central to Peralta's wealth creation, but it is not a current holding. The SEC filing states that the Peralta Group sold its remaining 34.5% interest to Vodafone in 2001, so current industry is classified from IUSA manufacturing.

TecNM and Líderes Mexicanos describe systems-engineering study at Instituto ICM de México, while Expansión reports engineering at Universidad Iberoamericana. Education is not proposed as a detail or included in the biographies because the institutions conflict.

No exact personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, YouTube, TikTok or personal website was verified. The exact X handle and official company website are proposed; company-run Facebook accounts are not represented as personal profiles.

Forbes has exact-name reporting and historical billionaire-list coverage, but no dedicated current personal profile was found. Article and list URLs are therefore research sources rather than a proposed Forbes social/profile URL.

review.notes:
Identity is very-high confidence and the biography is independent of the vessel record. The dossier distinguishes father-founded family wealth, Peralta's operating expansion through Iusacell, the completed telecom exit, current IUSA manufacturing holdings and active board, foundation and baseball leadership. Exact current personal shareholding remains private, so asset claims stay at company or family-group level. Nothing has been compiled, approved or applied.

Owner-tag consolidation research context: [1] Grupo IUSA: the father-founded industrial group Peralta inherited, materially expanded and still chairs, with a separate professional director general. [2] Electrical-products manufacturing: IUSA's documented current platform spans conductors, copper products, power equipment, meters, valves and controls, but no sufficiently exact active catalogue tag exists. [3] Iusacell: the mobile operator Peralta created within the family group, expanded with Bell Atlantic and exited through a strategic stake sale. [4] Mexiteleféricos: a transport-infrastructure company Peralta co-founded, demonstrating later diversification beyond IUSA's manufacturing base. [5] Jaguares de Nayarit: the current professional-baseball club whose board Peralta chairs. [6] Fundación Alejo Peralta: the family foundation Peralta currently presides over, with a separate director general.
